properties.Descriptio: In the Mojave Desert, along the southeastern border of the Cahuilla Basin, a structural depression in southeastern California.
properties.Sand_sourc: Sand derived from Colorado River sediments deposited in the basin containing Lake Cahuilla, rather than surrounding mountains (a).
properties.Sand_chara: Felsic: quartz (~60%), feldspar (~40%) (b). Quartz (72%), plagioclase (12%), potassium feldspar (7%), graphite/magnetite/spinel (8%) (c).
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press. b:

properties.Descriptio: Expansive dune field and sand sheet on the northern coast of the Gulf of California.
properties.Sand_sourc: Source material from the Ancestral Colorado River, contemporaneous influx from the lower Colorado River valley and coastal influx from the Bahia del Adair inlet (a).
properties.Sand_chara: Dominant mineral phase is quartz, with a minor amount of feldspar. Biotite and volcanic rock fragments are found in the east and northeast portions of the dune field, shell fragments and foraminiferal are found near the coast (c).
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press. b:

properties.Descriptio: Barchan dune field on the southwestern coast of the Salton Sea, in the Mojave Desert.
properties.Sand_sourc: Lake Cahuilla sediments (a); late Cenozoic sedimentary rocks from the San Felipe Hills (b).
properties.Approximat: Between 10 and 70 m below sea level (c)
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press.  b:

properties.Descriptio: In the Mojave Desert, two roughly parallel transport pathways through the Bristol Trough and the Palen Playa, northeast of the Salton Sea.
properties.Sand_sourc: Varied local sediment (sands are immature and geochemically distinct from mature Grand Canyon sands) (a).
properties.Sand_chara: Plagioclase is dominant phase (~60%), followed by potassium feldspar (~30%), and quartz (~10%) (b).
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press. b:

properties.Descriptio: East of the Colorado River, in west-central Arizona.
properties.Sand_sourc: Sourced from the Colorado River (a,b).
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press. b:

properties.Descriptio: Within the Mojave National Preserve.
properties.Sand_sourc: Sands from the Mojave River are blown onto the western side of the Cady Mtns. These sands also feed into the Kelso dunes (a).
properties.Sand_chara: Mineralogy is complex. Identified quartz, potassium feldspar, plagioclase, hornblende, sphene, tremolite, epidote, biotite, and small fragments of fine volcanic rock (c).
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press. b:

properties.Descriptio: In the Mojave Desert. A major OHV site for southern California, therefore little detailed surface morphology remains undisturbed.
properties.Sand_sourc: Sourced from the deflation of Pleistocene deposits associated with Lake Manly in southern Death Valley. A minor amount of material has resulted from deflation of the smaller Lake Dumont in Silurian Valley, as well as Kingston wash, which enters the valle
properties.Sand_chara: Quartz, potassium feldspar, and plagioclase (d).
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press. b:

properties.Descriptio: Within the Wilderness section of the Death Valley National Park.
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press.

properties.Descriptio: Within Death Valley National Park. A plant found only on these dunes makes the Eureka Dunes one of the most protected areas within the park.
properties.Sand_sourc: Possible local alluvial system (c).
properties.Sand_chara: Coarse-grained quartz-dominant sand that is both non-sodic and non-saline (b).
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press. b:

properties.Descriptio: Located in the Amargosa Desert of southwestern Nevada.
properties.Sand_sourc: Nearby playa deposits (a).
properties.Sand_chara: Quartz (20%), plagioclase (35%), potassium feldspar (20%), calcite/dolomite (1%), clay minerals (3%), amorphous and or opal cristobalite (20%) (d).
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press. b:

properties.Descriptio: Located in the southern potion of Clayton Valley, ~7 miles south of Silver Peak, Nevada.
properties.Sand_sourc: Local origin, derived from deflation of playa and alluvial fan deposits (a).
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press. b:

properties.Descriptio: Sand Mountain Recreational Area of Nevada.
properties.Sand_sourc: Sediments are derived from materials deposited within nearby glacial Lake Lahontan (a).
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press. b:

properties.Descriptio: Area north of Winnemucca, Nevada. Also known as Silver State Dune Complex due to sand transport occurring across two mountain ranges.
properties.Sand_sourc: Sediments source is Lake Lahontan (a). Derived from multiple local sources, including metamorphic, plutonic, and volcanic bedrock in a similar manner than that observed in the Mojave Desert (b,c).
properties.Sand_chara: Quartz (20 - 68%), feldspar (80 - 32%, mostly albite), lithic fragments comprising 45% or more and vary between the different basins crossed by the dune field (b,c).
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press. b:

properties.Descriptio: Little Sahara National Recreation Area, Utah.
properties.Sand_sourc: Most sediments are sourced from deposits left by the Sevier River, which used to flow into Lake Bonneville (a).
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press. b:

properties.Descriptio: Coral Pink Sand Dunes State Park, Utah
properties.Sand_sourc: Sediment source is the Navajo Sandstone
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press.

properties.Descriptio: Northeastern Arizona
properties.Sand_sourc: Sourced from the Little Colorado River, also sand eroding from local outcrops within drainage basins (b).
properties.Sand_chara: Dominantly quartz sand, with varied quantities of silt and clay (up to 15% in basal parts of sampled linear dunes) (b).
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press. b:

properties.Descriptio: White Sands National Park, situated within the Tularosa Basin of the Rio Grande Rift.
properties.Sand_sourc: Deflation from Lake Lucero, but initially leached from rocks in the surrounding mountains (a). Deflation of evaporite beds of Lake Otero and the younger playa lakes (e.g., Lake Lucero) (b).
properties.Sand_chara: Gypsum, trace quartz grains (b). Quartz (1%),  gypsum and/or sylvite-halite (99%) (f).
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press. b:

properties.Descriptio: Great Sand Dune National Park and Preserve, situated near the eastern margin of the northern San Luis Valley in southcentral Colorado.
properties.Dune_type: C, S, TR, B, P, SS
properties.Sand_sourc: Initially Rio Grande (increased water supply from melting glaciers); San Juan Mountains (c). ~70% from the San Juan Mtns, ~30% from the Sangre de Cristo Mountains (d).
properties.Sand_chara: Quartz (29%), feldspar (8.9%), other rock fragments (57.9%) by volume (f). Quartz (16%), plagioclase (63%), potassium feldspar (12%) , calcite/dolomite (2%), graphite/magnetite/spinel (4%), amphibole (2.3% ), amorphous and/or opal cristobalite ( 1%) (g).
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press. b:

properties.Descriptio: Southwestern Wyoming.
properties.Sand_sourc: Derived from the Eocene Green River Formation, not from local glacio-fluvial deposits (a).
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press. b:

properties.Descriptio: Eastern portion of the Snake River Plain in southern Idaho, near the town of St. Anthony.
properties.Dune_type: P, TR, B, BR, CL, C
properties.Sand_sourc: Derived from local sediments deposited into nearby Mud Lake (a vestige of Lake Terreton) (a). Deposits of glacial Lake Terreton (Pleistocene age) (c).
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press. b:

properties.Descriptio: Central Idaho, collected in an abandoned cutoff meander of the Snake River, carved into the basalt of the Snake River Plain.
properties.Sand_sourc: Derived from surrounding basalts (basaltic grains) (a). From Bruneau and Glenns Ferry Formation (b).
properties.Sand_chara: Quartz, feldspar, and basaltic particles (12% vol of material) (b). Quartz (50% ), plagioclase (28%), potassium feldspar ( 12%), amorphous and/or opal cristobalite (10% ) (c).
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press. b:

properties.Field_Site: Shifting Sands dune field/Christmas Valley sand dunes
properties.Descriptio: Northeast of Christmas Valley, in southcentral Oregon.
properties.Sand_sourc: The drying of Lake Chewaucan (a). Sand deflated from Fort Rock Lake (Pleistocene), sand-sized tephra deposited by eruptions for Mt. Mazama (b).
properties.Sand_chara: Volcanic glass and devitrified glass fragments (10-30%), plagioclase (50%), basaltic lithic fragments, aggregates of silt and clay-sized volcanic ash, pyroxenes, opaque minerals (mostly magnetite), and trace occurrences of fossil fragments and other mine
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press. b:

properties.Descriptio: Southwest of Moses Lake, central Washington.
properties.Sand_sourc: Basalts and granodiorite outcrops within the Channeled Scablands, caused by massive floods from glacial Lake Missoula are likely the source, not the local Columbia River (a).
properties.Sand_chara: Basalt fragments (60-80%), quartz (20-40%) by volume (b).
properties.References: a: Zimbelman and Williams (2007) Eolian dunes and deposits in the western United States as analogs to wind-related features on Mars, in The Geology of Mars: Evidence from Earth-based Analogs, ed. Mary Chapman, published by Cambridge University Press. b:

properties.Descriptio: Southeast Iran.
properties.References: a: Foroutan and Zimbelman (2016) Mega-ripples in Iran: A new analog for transverse aeolian ridges on Mars, Icarus v. 274, pg. 99-105.

properties.Descriptio: Puna of Argentina
properties.Sand_sourc: Pumice clasts are sourced from local ignimbrites, gravels are locally derived and were available as lag on the surface of the host ignimbrite (a).
properties.Sand_chara: Bimodal; lithics (volcanic and metamorphic) and pumice clasts  (a).
properties.References: a: de Silva et al (2013) Gravel-mantled megaripples of the Argentinean Puna: A model for their origin and growth with implications for Mars, GSA Bulletin, v. 125, no 11/12, pg. 1912-1929.

properties.Descriptio: Puna of Argentina
properties.Sand_sourc: Pumice clasts are sourced from local ignimbrites, gravels are locally derived and were available as lag on the surface of the host ignimbrite (a).
properties.Sand_chara: Dominated by dark gravels that reflect the dominance of andesitic lava and vitrophyric fragments (a).
properties.References: a: de Silva et al (2013) Gravel-mantled megaripples of the Argentinean Puna: A model for their origin and growth with implications for Mars, GSA Bulletin, v. 125, no 11/12, pg. 1912-1929.

properties.Descriptio: Puna of Argentina
properties.Sand_sourc: Red-brown clasts from Upper Miocene Rosada ignimbrite. Pumice clasts are sourced from local ignimbrites, gravels are locally derived and were available as lag on the surface of the host ignimbrite (a).
properties.Sand_chara: Ignimbrite, quartz-rich Paleozoic basement, andesite clasts (a).
properties.References: a: de Silva et al (2013) Gravel-mantled megaripples of the Argentinean Puna: A model for their origin and growth with implications for Mars, GSA Bulletin, v. 125, no 11/12, pg. 1912-1929.

properties.Descriptio: Within the Puna of Argentina, on the shores of the Salar de Incahuasi playa.
properties.Sand_sourc: Pumice clasts are sourced from local ignimbrites, gravels are locally derived and were available as lag on the surface of the host ignimbrite (a).
properties.Sand_chara: Clasts of Rosada ignimbrite, older metamorphic basement rocks, and andesite (a).
properties.References: a: de Silva et al (2013) Gravel-mantled megaripples of the Argentinean Puna: A model for their origin and growth with implications for Mars, GSA Bulletin, v. 125, no 11/12, pg. 1912-1929.

properties.Descriptio: Puna of Argentina, east of Campo Piedra Pomez
properties.Sand_sourc: Pumice clasts are sourced from local ignimbrites, gravels are locally derived and were available as lag on the surface of the host ignimbrite (a).
properties.Sand_chara: Basement milky quartz clasts are the dominant phase (a).
properties.References: a: de Silva et al (2013) Gravel-mantled megaripples of the Argentinean Puna: A model for their origin and growth with implications for Mars, GSA Bulletin, v. 125, no 11/12, pg. 1912-1929.

properties.Descriptio: Situated on the seaward fringe of the Sigatoka River delta.
properties.Sand_sourc: Sourced from the Sigatoka River (a).
properties.Sand_chara: Bimodal: Mafic minerals (amphiboles, pyroxenes, olivine, mica: 32%), Opaque (metallic, 9%), quartz (20%), feldspar (14%) by volume (b).
properties.References: a: Dickinson et al (1998) Geomorphic an archaeological landscapes of the Sigatoka Dune site. Asian Perspectives, vol. 37, no. 1, pg. 1-31. b: Edgett, K.S., and Lancaster, N., 1993, Volcaniclastic aeolian dunes: Terrestrial examples and application to mar

properties.Descriptio: In the McMurdo Dry Valley system of Antarctica
properties.Sand_sourc: Sourced from the Onyx River (a).
properties.References: a: Gillies, J.A., Nickling, W.G., Tilson, M., and Furtak-Cole, E., 2012, Wind-formed gravel bed forms, Wright Valley, Antarctica: Journal of Geophysical Research, v. 117, F04017, doi:10.1029/2012JF002378.

properties.Descriptio: Within the Negev Desert.
properties.Sand_sourc: Sourced from the Uvda Valley (a).
properties.Sand_chara: Calcite (60%) and quartz (35%) (a).
properties.References: a: Yizhaq, H., O. Isenberg, R. Wenkart, H. Tsaor, and A. Karnieli (2008), Morphology and dynamics of aeolian mega-ripples in Nahal Kasuy, southern Israel, Isr. J. Earth Sci., 57, 149– 165, doi:10.1560/IJES.57.3-4.149.

properties.Descriptio: Northwest China.
properties.Sand_sourc: Sourced from the Altyn Tagh mountains (b).
properties.References: a: Qian, G., Z. Dong, Z. Zhang, W. Luo, and J. Lu (2012), Granule ripples in the Kumtagh Desert, China: Morphology, grain size and influencing factors, Sedimentology, 59, 1888– 1901, doi:10.1111/j.1365-3091.2012.01330.x. b: Dong et al. (2010)

properties.Descriptio: Located on the northern edge of the Kumtagh Sand Sea, northwest China.
properties.Dune_type: B, L, MR, CL, G, Y
properties.Sand_sourc: Beishan Mountain piedmont, alluvial-diluvial materials and denudation products (a).
properties.References: a: Yang et al 2021, Migration of barchan dunes and factors that influence migration in the Sanlongsha dune field of the northern Kumtagh Sand Sea, China. Geomorphology, v. 378.

properties.Descriptio: Located on the Alxa Plateau in north-central China, within a wide dry valley formed by an ancient river.
properties.Sand_sourc: From an ancient river that carved the valley the dunes are located in (river estimated to date back to 10,000 yrs. ago) (a).
properties.References: a: Yao et al (2007) Migration of sand dunes on the northern Alxa Plateau, Inner Mongolia, China. Journal of Arid Environments v. 70, pg. 80-93.

properties.Descriptio: Navajo Nation, northeast Arizona.
properties.Sand_sourc: Felsic material sourced from Little Colorado River sediments and mafic material is from local ash deposits from the San Francisco Volcanic Field (a).
properties.Sand_chara: Bimodal: felsic (quartz) and mafic (basaltic grains) (a).
properties.References: a: Bogle et al (2015) Field measurement and analysis of climatic factors affecting dune mobility near Grand Falls on the Navajo Nation, southwestern United States. Geomorphology, v. 228, pg. 41-51.

properties.Descriptio: Southeastern Qatar.
properties.Sand_sourc: Sediments sourced from an area now under the Persian Sea that was previously exposed during a Pleistocene sea level low stand (a).
properties.Sand_chara: Silica grains, with smaller amounts of calcareous fragments, argillaceous dust and trace amounts of heavy minerals (b).
properties.References: a: Michel et al (2018) Comparing dune migration measured from remote sensing with sand flux prediction based on weather data and model, a test case in Qatar, Earth and Planetary Letters, v. 497, pg. 12-21. 2Embabi and Ashour (1993) Barchan dunes in Qatar

properties.Descriptio: Located in the mountainous coastal region of southern Victoria Land, Antarctica.
properties.Dune_type: B, BR, CL, WB, SS, TR
properties.Sand_sourc: Sediment source is the Lower Victoria Valley outwash glacio-fluvial sediments with additional sediment contributions from the weathering of exposed bedrock and erratic boulders (a).
properties.References: a: Bourke et al (2009) Sand dune movement in the Victoria Valley, Antarctica, Geomorphology, v. 109, pg. 148-160.

properties.Descriptio: South-central Wyoming, in a topographically regulated \"corridor\" of high wind.
properties.Sand_sourc: Derived primarily from the Tertiary Battle Spring Formation (a).
properties.Sand_chara: Quartz (66%) and feldspar (34%) (a).
properties.References: a: Gaylord, D.R. (1982) Geologic history of the Ferris Dune Field, south-central Wyoming, GSA Special Paper, v. 192, pg. 65-82. b: Stokes and Gaylord (1993) Optical dating of Holocene dune sands in the Ferris Dune Field, Wyoming. Quaternary Research, v.

properties.Descriptio: Simpson Desert, forming the 'red center' of the continent.
properties.Sand_sourc: Divided into two groups: Sand group 1 is located in the SE of Simpson Desert and is thought to have been derived from deflation of flood flats associated with major rivers and salt lake systems. Sand group 2 is in the northern and western Simpson desert
properties.Sand_chara: Iron oxide stains the grains red in color (a).
properties.References: a: R. D. Lorenz and J. R. Zimbelman, Dune Worlds, Springer Praxis Books, DOI: 10.1007/978-3-540-89725-5_1, Springer-Verlag Berlin Heidelberg 2014. b: Craddock et al. (2015) Temporal observations of a linear sand dune in the Simpson Desert, central Austra

properties.Descriptio: Area is northeast of Dyngjujökull and is bordered to the north by the Askja volcano and to the east by the major glacial drainage system of the Jökulsá á Fjöllum and by the Vaðalda shield volcano.
properties.Sand_sourc: Primary source is Dyngjujökull (outlet glacier). In summer, ablation of the glacier feeds a number of outlet streams. Due to percolation, downstream transmission losses occur and results in the accumulation of sand available for aeolian transport at the
properties.Sand_chara: Dominated by glass grains (80-90%). Remaining fractions corresponds to a few percent of olivine, pyroxene, and plagioclase. Overall, glass grains comprise ~80% of sand and crystalline phases ~20% (a).
properties.References: a: Baratoux et al. (2011) Volcanic sands of Iceland: Diverse origins of aeolian sand deposits revealed at Dyngjusandur and Lambahraun. Earth Surface Processes and Landforms, v. 36, no. 13, pg. 1789-1808.

properties.Descriptio: Sandy areas of the Lambahraun lava flows are located south of the Hagafellsjökull.
properties.Sand_sourc: Hyaloclastite ridges, sediments deposited by the glaciers and Eldborgir lava flows (a).
properties.Sand_chara: Olivine (~15-20%), plagioclase and pyroxene (30%). Overall, crystalline phases ~80% and glass ~20% (a).
properties.References: a: Baratoux et al. (2011) Volcanic sands of Iceland: Diverse origins of aeolian sand deposits revealed at Dyngjusandur and Lambahraun. Earth Surface Processes and Landforms, v. 36, no. 13, pg. 1789-1808.

properties.Descriptio: Located at the northwestern edge of the region influenced by the East Asian Monsoon, near the lower reaches of the Heihe River. Second largest area of shifting sands in China.
properties.Sand_sourc: Originated in alluvial deposits of the Heihe River west of the sand sea (a).
properties.References: a: Dong et al. (2013) Investigation of the sand sea with the tallest dunes on Earth: China's Badain Jaran Sand Sea. Earth-Science Reviews, v. 120, pg. 20-39.

properties.Descriptio: Altiplano-Atacama desert region, dry desert without vegetation and soil.
properties.Sand_chara: Bright pumice grains, clay minerals, carbonate, aragonite, and talc (water-related alteration minerals) (a).
properties.References: a: Kereszturi et al. (2022) Wind-snow interactions at the Ojos del Salado region as a potential Mars analogue site in the Altiplano-Atacama desert region. Icarus, v. 378.

properties.Descriptio: Located on the western flank of Kilauea, an active basaltic shield volcano. Area remains a desert because of low annual precipitation and toxic gases released from the central pit caldera.
properties.Sand_sourc: Keanakako'i Formation is the source of all basaltic material. Sands were derived from airfall ashes from phreatomagmatic eruptions of Kilauea and reworked lava (a).
properties.Sand_chara: High amount of volcanic glass fragments, lesser amounts of feldspar, olivine, and pyroxene (a).
properties.References: a: Tirsch et al. (2011) Spectral and petrologic analyses of basaltic sands in Ka'u Desert (Hawaii) - Implications for the dark dunes on Mars. Earth Surface Processes and Landforms, v. 37, no. 4, pg. 434-448.
